tagline.en: Make the subject and the verb match

subtitle.en: Every card has a short rule and 3 questions. Learn when a verb takes -s, and when to use is or are, has or have, was or were.
subtitle.bn: প্রতিটি কার্ডে ছোট্ট একটি নিয়ম আর ৩টি প্রশ্ন। শেখো কখন verb-এ -s বসে, আর কখন is বা are, has বা have, was বা were হয়।

hint.en: One person or thing, or many?

hint.bn: আগে আসল subject খুঁজে বের করো

rule.en: With one person or thing (he, she, it), the verb takes -s. With many (they), it does not.
rule.bn: একজন বা একটি (he, she, it) হলে verb-এ -s বসে; অনেক (they) হলে বসে না।

recap.example: My sister works. My sisters work.

options.why: “My sister” is one person (she), so the verb needs -s.
Don’t put “are” before a plain verb. Say “works”.
A sentence needs a full verb. “Working” alone needs “is”.

questions.explanation: My sister is “she”, so the verb takes -s: works.

options.why: -s is only for one (he, she, it). Birds are many.
For many birds, use “are singing”, not “is singing”.
A sentence needs a full verb: sing.

questions.explanation: “The birds” are many (they), so the verb has no -s.

options.why: “Children” is plural, so the verb has no -s.
“Does” is for one (he, she, it), not for children.
A sentence needs a full verb: drink.

questions.explanation: “Children” means many (they), so no -s: drink.

title.en: Is / Are, Has / Have, Does / Do
title.bn: Is / Are, Has / Have, Does / Do

rule.en: For one person or thing use is, has and does. For many (and for you) use are, have and do. With I, use am, have and do.
rule.bn: একজন/একটি হলে is, has, does; অনেক (আর you) হলে are, have, do। I-এর সাথে am, have, do।

recap.example: He has a cat. They have a dog.

options.why: “Is” is for one thing. Shoes are more than one.
“Am” only goes with I.
“Be” needs a helper like “will”. Here use “are”.

questions.explanation: “Shoes” are two (they), so use are.

options.why: “Have” is for I, you, we and they. She takes “has”.
“Haves” is not a word. Use has.
A sentence needs a full verb: has.

questions.explanation: With she (one person), use has.

options.why: “Do” is for I, you, we and they. One dog takes “Does”.
“Is” doesn’t go with a plain verb like “like”.
“Are” is for many, and it doesn’t go with a plain verb.

questions.explanation: “Your dog” is it (one), so the question starts with Does.

rule.en: In the past, use was with I, he, she and it. Use were with you, we and they.
rule.bn: অতীতে I, he, she, it-এর সাথে was; you, we, they-এর সাথে were।

recap.example: I was tired. We were tired.

options.why: “Were” is for you, we and they, not I.
“Am” is the present, but “yesterday” is past.
“Be” needs a helper. Use “was”.

questions.explanation: With I in the past, use was.

options.why: “You” never takes “was”. Use were.
“Is” is present and doesn’t go with you.
“Be” needs a helper. Use “were”.

questions.explanation: “You” always takes were, even for one person.

questions.prompt: The books ___ on the table this morning.

options.why: “Was” is for one thing. Books are many.
“Is” is present and for one thing.
“Be” needs a helper. Use “were”.

questions.explanation: Books are many, and it is the past: were.

rule.en: Words like “of the toys” can sit between the subject and the verb. Skip them: the verb matches the real subject.
rule.bn: Subject আর verb-এর মাঝে “of the toys”-এর মতো শব্দ থাকতে পারে। সেগুলো বাদ দিয়ে আসল subject-এর সাথে verb মেলাও।

recap.example: The box of toys is under the bed.

questions.prompt: The box of toys ___ under the bed.

options.why: “Toys” is not the subject. The box is one thing, so use is.
“Am” only goes with I.
“Be” needs a helper. Use “is”.

questions.explanation: The subject is “the box” (one), not “toys”.

questions.prompt: The students in my class ___ very kind.

options.why: “My class” is not the subject. The students are many: are.
“Am” only goes with I.
“Be” needs a helper. Use “are”.

questions.explanation: The subject is “the students” (many), not “class”.

questions.prompt: The colour of the flowers ___ bright.

options.why: “Flowers” is not the subject. The colour is one thing.
“Am” only goes with I.
“Have” doesn’t fit here. The colour is bright.

questions.explanation: The subject is “the colour” (one), so use is.

cards.badge: A and B → are · A or B → nearest

rule.en: Two subjects joined by “and” are plural. With “or” or “nor”, the verb matches the subject nearest to it.
rule.bn: “and” দিয়ে যুক্ত দুটি subject হলে verb বহুবচন। “or” বা “nor” হলে verb কাছের subject-এর সাথে মেলে।

recap.example: Rina and Tom are here. Either Tom or his sisters are here.

options.why: “Rina and Tom” are two people, so use are.
“Am” only goes with I.
“Be” needs a helper. Use “are”.

questions.explanation: Two people joined by “and” make they: are.

questions.prompt: Either my mum or my dad ___ me to school.

options.why: With “or”, the verb matches “my dad” (one person), so it needs -s.
A sentence needs a full verb: takes.
Don’t put “are” before a plain verb.

questions.explanation: With “or”, match the nearest subject: “my dad” (he) → takes.

questions.prompt: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ ready.

options.why: The nearest subject is “the students”, which is plural.
“Am” only goes with I.
“Was” is for one. The students are many.

questions.explanation: With “nor”, match the nearest subject: “the students” (many) → are.

rule.en: Each, every, everyone, everybody and nobody take a singular verb, as if they were “he” or “she”.
rule.bn: Each, every, everyone, everybody, nobody-এর সাথে একবচন verb বসে (he/she-এর মতো)।

recap.example: Everyone is here. Each child has a book.

options.why: “Each” means one at a time, so use has.
A sentence needs a full verb: has.
“Are” is plural, and it doesn’t mean “own”.

questions.explanation: “Each” is singular, so use has.

options.why: “Everyone” takes a singular verb with -s.
“Everyone” is singular, so it would be “is”, not “are”.
A sentence needs a full verb: loves.

questions.explanation: “Everyone” is singular: loves.

questions.prompt: Every boy and girl ___ a prize.

options.why: After “every”, the verb is singular, even with “and”.
Don’t put “are” before a plain verb.
A sentence needs a full verb: gets.

questions.explanation: “Every” makes the whole subject singular, even with “and”: gets.

cards.badge: news / maths / a pair of + is

rule.en: Some words end in -s but are singular: news, maths, physics. “A pair of …” is singular too.
rule.bn: কিছু শব্দ -s দিয়ে শেষ হলেও একবচন: news, maths, physics। “A pair of …”-ও একবচন।

recap.example: The news is good. A pair of shoes is under the bed.

options.why: “News” looks plural but is singular.
“News” is singular, so never “were”.
“Am” only goes with I.

questions.explanation: “News” is singular, even though it ends in -s.

options.why: Mathematics is one subject, so use is.
“Am” only goes with I.
“Were” is plural and past.

questions.explanation: A school subject ending in -s (maths, physics) is singular.

questions.prompt: A pair of scissors ___ on the desk.

options.why: The subject is “a pair”, which is singular.
“Am” only goes with I.
“Were” is plural. One pair takes is or was.

questions.explanation: “A pair” is one pair, so use is.

cards.badge: there is + one · there are + many

rule.en: After “there”, look at the noun that comes next. One thing (or something you can’t count) → is. Many things → are.
rule.bn: “there”-এর পরের noun দেখো। একটি (বা গোনা যায় না এমন) হলে is, অনেক হলে are।

recap.example: There is a cat. There are three cats.

questions.prompt: There ___ a cat on the roof.

options.why: “A cat” is one cat. Use is.
“Am” only goes with I.
We say “There is”, not “There have”.

questions.explanation: “A cat” is one, so use is.

questions.prompt: There ___ three apples in the basket.

options.why: Three apples are more than one. Use are.
“Am” only goes with I.
We say “There are”, not “There has”.

questions.explanation: “Three apples” are many, so use are.

questions.prompt: There ___ some milk in the fridge.

options.why: You can’t count milk, so it is singular: is.
“Am” only goes with I.
Milk can’t be counted, so it takes is (or was), never were.

questions.explanation: “Milk” can’t be counted, so it takes is.
